AstroHelm continuously plate-solves the sky to guide you directly to galaxies, nebulae, planets, and stars—or precisely frame them for photography. No GoTo mount or proprietary hardware required. Free to use. No subscription. New to astronomy? A telescope opens up the wonders of the night sky — but getting started can be surprisingly difficult. What should you look at? How do you find it? What if you don't know the constellations? AstroHelm comes with a curated list of great objects to observe and highlights the best ones for your location and time. From bright planets to faint galaxies and nebulae, AstroHelm helps you find what’s worth seeing. Choose an object and AstroHelm shows you which way to move your telescope. Your phone’s camera recognizes the stars overhead and continuously determines where your telescope is pointing with high precision, ensuring the object lands right in your eyepiece. No need to learn star hopping or memorize constellations. And unlike a GoTo mount, there’s no complicated multi-star alignment. Better yet, AstroHelm can find its way even under heavily light-polluted skies. Live Plate Solving Traditional astronomy apps rely on your phone's compass and gyroscope, which drifts and lags. AstroHelm takes a picture of the night sky and matches it against a massive database of stars, so it always knows where you are pointing. Features Casual stargazers, serious amateur astronomers, and aspiring astrophotographers. AstroHelm is for everyone. Standard planetarium apps have pointing errors of several degrees, putting objects out of view. AstroHelm matches real stars in the sky to pinpoint your exact coordinates with sub-arcminute accuracy. The best dark-sky sites don't have Internet access. AstroHelm’s plate solving engine runs entirely on device. No internet connection required, and your camera images stay on your phone. AstroHelm works with equipment you already have, whether it's a dobsonian, a DIY telescope, or a telephoto lens. No lock-in. No proprietary hardware. Not sure what to observe? Discover rewarding targets for your location and tonight’s sky, taking altitude, twilight, and moonlight into consideration. Leave one device on your telescope and guide it from another in your hand, so you can explore the sky without reaching for the mounted screen. Works with astronomy software you already use, including Stellarium and SkySafari.
